headline: 1,400 Ohio truck jobs gone in a day
summary: On Wednesday nearly 1,400 people lost their jobs at what had been the Navistar truck factory in Springfield, Ohio. That wipes out about a year of job growth around Dayton. Trump holds a rally at a nearby high school on Saturday. Kyle Bos, 30, voted for him three times. He has a baby due in January and now knocks on doors for Democrats.
cover_answer: 1,400 paychecks. That's a year of new jobs around Dayton.
table_question: If a leader promises you money to vote for them, gift or bribe?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A big factory in Ohio that builds trucks told almost 1,400 people this week that it has no more work for them. That is enough people to fill a high school gym. Their families are working out what comes next, and the president is visiting nearby on Saturday to talk about jobs. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A gym full of people, and the grown-ups on it.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them a gym full of people rather than a number, and no villain. Losing a job is a grown-up fear they catch from your face before your words, so it ends on who is handling it. Expect "could you lose your job?" Answer with what is true for your house.

8-12.script: All year the Dayton area added jobs. On Wednesday one truck factory in Springfield cut nearly 1,400, about a year's worth, in a day. The area has lost about half of its 90,000 factory jobs since 1990. Saturday the president rallies nearby. Jobs are a scoreboard, and a town just lost a year of points.
8-12.why: Add all year, lose it in a day. A scoreboard they can read.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script runs the chain: one factory, 1,400 paychecks, a year of growth erased, in a region that has lost half its factory jobs since 1990. The scoreboard is the mechanism: points added slowly, taken off at once. Expect "why did they cut the jobs?" The report does not say. Say so.

13-17.script: Kyle Bos voted for Trump three times. Wednesday he lost his job with nearly 1,400 others. Saturday Trump rallies nearby, saying the economy is better than people think. Does a leader own a layoff on their watch? Second: Trump promises $5,000 checks if Republicans win. Bos calls it a bribe. Is it?
13-17.why: A voter who switched, a check on offer. Two live questions.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a president does not run a truck plant, and this president is asking for credit for the economy. The script hands them a voter who switched sides and a $5,000 promise and lets them argue where a bribe begins. Expect "is it his fault?" Not the layoff. The claim that things are better is his.

5-7.q: Will the people get new jobs?
5-7.a: Many will, and it can take a while. One dad in the story has a baby coming in January, so his family is planning hard right now.

8-12.a: Nearly 1,400 jobs is about a year of new jobs around Dayton.

8-12.q: Why did the factory cut the jobs?
8-12.a: The report doesn't say. Dayton has lost half its factory jobs since 1990.

13-17.a: He doesn't run the plant. But he's asking for credit for the economy.
Money promised for a vote. Bos says bribe. Others might say relief.
